definitions.explanation: The spring season of the coming year. Slightly formal/literary; common in news, business, and graduation/employment contexts since the Japanese school and fiscal year begins in spring.

examples.japanese: {来春|らいしゅん}⟦{卒業|そつぎょう}→卒業：01643_sotsugyou⟧⟦します→する：00392_suru⟧。
{来春|らいしゅん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧だ。
examples.english: I plan to start working at a new company next spring.

examples.japanese: {来春|らいしゅん}⟦{開業|かいぎょう}→開業：14570_kaigyou⟧⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中心|ちゅうしん}→中心：01467_chuushin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{建設|けんせつ}→建設：02708_kensetsu⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The new station scheduled to open next spring is being built in the center of town.

notes:
Composed of {来|らい} (coming) + {春|しゅん} (spring, Sino-Japanese reading). The native equivalent is ⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧, which is more conversational; {来春|らいしゅん} sounds slightly literary or formal.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {来春|らいしゅん}⟦{卒業|そつぎょう}→卒業：01643_sotsugyou⟧: graduating next spring
- {来春|らいしゅん}⟦{入社|にゅうしゃ}→入社：03131_nyuusha⟧: joining a company next spring
- {来春|らいしゅん}⟦{開業|かいぎょう}→開業：14570_kaigyou⟧ / ⟦{開店|かいてん}→開店：14569_kaiten⟧: opening next spring
- {来春|らいしゅん}⟦{予定|よてい}→予定：00824_yotei⟧: scheduled for next spring

USAGE:
Frequently appears in news headlines, press releases, and recruiting language. In everyday conversation, ⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧ is more natural.
